# Mesh, layout, exchange and multi-block runs {#sec-ch13}

A Mesh is the set of blocks that one process advances together. This chapter describes how blocks are placed and
numbered (the layout), how their ghost cells are filled from each other (the exchange), how the blocks of one
process meet while they do so, and what changes when the blocks' stages run as CUDA graphs. What a ghost cell
holds, and the geometry of panel seams, are the subject of @sec-ch03. How a single block's stage is split into
segments and captured is @sec-ch11. The schemes are listed in @tbl-ch13-schemes.

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| layouts and ranks (@sec-ch13-layouts) | `distribute: layout`, `nb1`-`nb3`, `blocks_per_process` | `slab`, one block | n/a (a map) | `test_local_horizontal_cells` |
| the ghost exchange and the same-process waits (@sec-ch13-ghost) | `blocks_per_process` | one block per process | exact copy | `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` |
| exchange cuts and multi-block capture (@sec-ch13-cuts) | `integration: execution` | `auto` | exact (graph equals eager) | `test_graph_mesh_many_blocks` |
| Mesh-agree (@sec-ch13-agree) | none (a rule) | on with more than one block | exact (graph equals eager) | `test_mesh_disagree` |
| the x1 seam split (@sec-ch13-x1split) | `distribute: nb1` | `nb1: 1` | exact copy at the seam | `test_x1_seam_split` |

: The schemes of this chapter. Test names omit the `.release` and `_python` suffixes of their ctest entries.
{#tbl-ch13-schemes}
